quick-rules.title: How to Play
quick-rules.placeholder: Quick rules will be added here.

spending-power.title: Spending Power
spending-power.placeholder: Effect and Power guidance will be added here.

tags.title: This Game Runs on Tags
tags.body: Short descriptors that say what’s true and give Power to or weaken your Hero’s actions: [@t handsome], [@t spell of slumber], [@tw old injury], [@s charmed].

themes.title: Themes
themes.body:
Related sets of tags and Quests. Your Hero has four themes, each with:

[@t Power tags](inc. the theme's title tag)Positive tags that give Power to your actions. They can be temporarily scratched , making them unusable until recovered.
[@tw Weakness tags]Negative tags that decrease the Power of your actions. However, they allow you to mark Improve on the theme.
QuestA motivation for the theme, something your Hero seeks, defends, or upholds.

storyTags.title: Story Tags
storyTags.body:
Temporary tags which can be positive or negative based on the situation, like [@t staff] or [@t vantage point].

  • Removed when scratched .
  • Expire with time.
  • Recorded in backpack (if yours) or a Tracking Card (if general).

statuses.title: Statuses
statuses.body:
Tags that describe conditions with a tier from 1 (mild) to 6 (deadly or transformative), like [@s wounded-3] or [@s glad-2].

  • Recorded on Tracking Cards. Write the status tag and mark its tier on the card.
  • Stacking: If you gain the same or a similar status again, mark the new tier on the same card. If the box for that tier is already marked, mark the box to its right. The highest marked tier is the current tier.
  • Reducing: Move all the marked boxes a number of slots to the left; remove the status if it falls below 1.
  • Limits: At tier 5, you are overcome by the status. At tier 6, it kills or transforms you.

development.title: Hero Development
development.body:
Mark Improve whenever one of your weakness tags is invoked. At 3 Improve, the theme gets an Improvement (usually, a new power tag).

Mark Abandon whenever you ignore or betray your Quest. At 3 Abandon, your theme is replaced.

Mark a Milestone whenever you achieve a goal of your Quest. At 3 Milestones, your theme evolves.

Replacing or evolving a theme gains you Promise, which unlocks greater Moments of Fulfillment.

fellowship.title: The Fellowship
fellowship.body:
A shared theme usable by any of the Heroes.

[@t Power tags]Single-use (scratched when invoked; cannot be burnt for Power). Recovered during camping.
[@tw Weakness tags]Mark Improve on the Fellowship theme when invoked.
[@t Relationship tags]Single-use story tags (positive or negative), one for each other Hero. Recreated during camping.

scene.title: During a Scene
scene.body: Repeat the game loop — Establish – Action – Consequences — until the stakes are won, lost, or deferred, or the scene otherwise concludes. Continue to the next scene or to camping.

establish.title: Establish
establish.body:
The Narrator…

  • (Re)describes the scene.
  • Highlights the stakes (why this scene matters).
  • Introduces Challenges.
  • Makes Threats (actions initiated by Challenges).
  • Asks the player(s) “What do you do?” and gives the spotlight to a Hero (a different Hero each turn).

action.title: Action
action.body:
The Hero in the spotlight describes their action.

The Narrator chooses how to determine the outcome:

  • Simple (Narrator’s call).
  • Quick (Roll).
  • Detailed (Roll + Spend).

consequences.title: Consequences
consequences.body:
The Narrator can deliver Consequences if

  • A Threat was ignored (a Challenge action materializes).
  • The Hero’s action (roll) had Consequences.
  • The Narrator invokes a Hero’s weakness tag for Consequences (the Hero marks Improve).

The Narrator decides on Consequences

  • Narrative.
  • Give or scratch any number of tags, or give or reduce a status of any tier. The Hero may react.

camping.title: Camping
camping.body:
The Narrator expires story tags.

Each Hero chooses 2 activities (or 3 with Consequences):

  • REST: Recover some statuses and scratched power tags (Narrator’s call).
  • REFLECT: Mark Improve on one theme.
  • CAMP ACTION: Count Power and spend half of it without rolling (rounded up), or roll.

Each Hero chooses to recover a Fellowship power tag or create a new relationship tag with another Hero.

challenges.title: Challenges
challenges.body:
Adversaries, obstacles, and dangers that put your Hero or their goals at risk.

Challenges act against you by making Threats during Establish and delivering Consequences.

You overcome Challenges with a Success (Quick), or by giving them statuses high enough to max their Limits, e.g. [@s harm-4], [@s banish-2], or [@s convince-3] (Detailed), Narrator’s choice.

roll.title: Making a Roll
roll.body:
Count the action’s Power.

Invoke relevant tags and statuses of the Hero, the target, the environment, etc.

  • +1/−1 Power for every positive/negative tag.
  • +3 Power for scratching a Hero’s positive tag.
  • +/− tier of best and worst status.
  • +/−3 Power if Favored/Imperiled due to Might (+/−6 if Extremely).

Mark Improve for every invoked weakness tag.

Roll two six-sided dice (2d6) and add Power.

spendingPower.title: Spending Power
spendingPower.body:
Spend your Power on your action’s Effects (spend 1 when Power is 0 or less):

  • Add, scratch , or recover a tag (2 Power).
  • Give or reduce a status (1 Power per tier).
  • Discover a valuable detail (1 Power).
  • Extra feat in addition to other Effects (1 Power).
  • Add a single-use tag with the last 1 Power.

reaction.title: Reaction
reaction.body:
If the Narrator allows it, the Hero can take a reaction to lessen Consequences at the cost of 1 Power per status tier and 2 Power per tag.

Describe, count Power, and roll as in Detailed.

  • 10 or more (or ): Spend Power+1 on any Effect.
  • 7–9: Spend Power only to lessen.
  • 6 or less (or ): Take Consequences as-is.

spendingPowerPage.subtitle: on Effects
spendingPowerPage.intro:
When you succeed in a Detailed action, spend the action’s Power on game Effects. Every Effect must match the described action; you may mix and match Effects when they fit.

Minimum 1: on a Success, you always have at least 1 Power to spend, even if the action’s Power is zero or less.
spendingPowerPage.costs:
• Add or scratch a tag — 2 Power.
  • Add or reduce a status — 1 Power per tier.
  • Discover a valuable detail — 1 Power.
  • Perform an Extra Feat — 1 Power, but only after spending Power on a tag, status, or discovery.
  • Create a single-use story tag — 1 Power, if you have only 1 Power left.
spendingPowerPage.examplesTitle: Examples of Tag and Status Effects
spendingPowerPage.examples:
Against an Opponent or Target

  • Attack — slash, punch, curse, shoot: give a harmful status such as [@s wounded] or [@s cursed].
  • Disrupt — blind, confuse, shock, trip, interrupt: give a hindering tag or status such as [@t weak spot] or [@s blinded].
  • Influence — convince, threaten, provoke, mind control: give a compelling status such as [@s convinced] or [@s intimidated].
  • Weaken — break, sunder, neutralize, silence: scratch a useful tag or reduce a useful status such as [@t shield] or [@s confident].

For Yourself or an Ally

  • Bestow — teach, empower, enchant, equip: give a new ability such as [@t keen hearing] or [@t spear training].
  • Create — craft, find, purchase, summon, rally: create an object or being such as [@t sturdy rope] or [@t summoned sentinel].
  • Enhance — assist, aim, boost, take cover: give a helpful status such as [@s aiming] or [@s protected].
  • Restore — heal, repair, rejuvenate, undo: reduce [@s wounded] or recover a scratched power tag such as [@t tough as oak].

On a Process

  • Advance — make progress, get closer, push forward: increase a status such as [@s thawing].
  • Set Back — delay, ruin, sabotage, reverse: reduce the progress status or create an opposing one such as [@s freezing].

Other Effects

  • Discover — sense, recall, research, converse: discover a valuable detail.
  • Extra Feat — achieve one additional minor result included in the action.
spendingPowerPage.extra:
An Extra Feat is a narrative achievement beyond the main Effect: a tag, status, or discovery. First spend at least some Power on a main Effect.

An Extra Feat can keep the spotlight for a follow-up action, prevent an incoming Threat for now, reach a good position, or add a special flair. For example, while fleeing an angry crowd, you could increase an [@s escaping] status and spend another Power to zig and zag so every rotten vegetable misses, preventing that Threat for now.
spendingPowerPage.reaction:
When Consequences create negative Effects, the Narrator may allow a Reaction. Count the Reaction’s Power and roll 2d6 + Power.

  • 6 or less: suffer the Consequences as-is.
  • 7–9: spend Power only to lessen Consequences — 1 Power cancels 1 status tier; 2 Power cancels a tag Effect.
  • 10 or more: gain +1 Power and spend your Power on any Effects—for example, counterattack or learn something about your enemy, if it fits the described Reaction.

You cannot invoke tags already used in the preceding action.
